content.text: Skip to ArticleCloseArtemis II splashdown: How to watch return to Earth liveUpdated: Apr. 10, 2026, 11:56 a.m.|Published: Apr. 10, 2026, 11:54 a.m.Earthset captured through the Orion spacecraft window at 6:41 p.m. EDT, April 6, 2026, during the Artemis II crew’s flyby of the Moon. A muted blue Earth with bright white clouds sets behind the cratered lunar surface.Courtesy NASABy Scott Turner | sturner@al.comThe Artemis II crew — NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch and CSA (Canadian Space Agency) astronaut Jeremy Hansen – are in the final hours of their 10-day journey to the moon and back.They will splash down in their Orion space capsule at about 7:07 p.m. Central Time in the Pacific Ocean off the coast near San Diego where a combined NASA and U.S. military recovery team will be standing by to welcome them home.READ MORE: How Alabama’s Marshall Space Flight Center is helping Artemis II’s moon missionPeople can watch the splashdown live on NASA+, Amazon Prime, Apple TV, Netflix, HBO Max, Discovery+, Peacock and Roku starting at 5:30 p.m. That is in addition to the watch party at Big Spring Park West hosted by the city of Huntsville and Downtown Huntsville, Inc.
